title: Task-switch costs - short session usability notes & backlog hypotheses
body:
Summary:
This note captures observations from 6 short (20-25 minute) moderated usability sessions focused on operator workflows that require frequent context switches: changing model variants, switching routes, checking cost/latency breakdowns, and responding to alerts. The goal was to surface micro-interaction friction, mental-model mismatches, and small copy/wireframe changes that reduce cognitive cost and error rate.

Method:
- Sessions: 6 participants (mix of ML engineers and platform engineers) recruited from existing beta customers and internal SEs.
- Format: Remote moderated using shared prototype (Figma) + console sandbox. Each participant ran 3 micro-tasks: 1) swap model variant for a routed endpoint under load, 2) set up a cost-safeguard rule for a route, 3) interpret a latency spike and run a fallback.
- Metrics captured: task completion (success/error), time-on-task, hesitation points (noted by moderator), verbalized confusion.
- Note style: quick scribbles, quotes, and verbatim frustrations preserved.

Participants:
- P1: Senior ML infra engineer (startup)
- P2: Platform engineer (mid-market SaaS)
- P3: Internal SRE (Redwood)
- P4: Solutions engineer (customer success)
- P5: ML engineer (enterprise pilot)
- P6: Developer (early-stage app)

Key observations (high level):
1) Context loss is the biggest friction. When switching model variants from the route detail screen, participants frequently lost the prior request/throughput baseline and hesitated to confirm the change. They wanted an inline comparison (delta, expected latency change).
2) Microcopy ambiguity around "variant" vs "model version" caused incorrect assumptions. Two participants thought variant implied a quantized version; one rolled back accidentally.
3) Cost and latency info are treated as a single decision signal. People wanted an explicit "expected unit-cost impact" shown next to variant selections and autoscale settings.
4) Fallback behavior mental models differ. Some expect the fallback to be automatic and invisible; others expect a visible routing event with logs. Lack of clarity led to unnecessary manual rollback attempts.
5) Small affordances matter: a persistent toast with "undo" for route changes reduced anxiety; absence increased calls to support.

Representative quotes:
- "I don't trust changing the variant unless I can see how it affected the last hour." (P2)
- "What's the difference between the blue and green model? Is one quantized?" (P5)
- "If latency spikes I want to know if the system already switched to fallback or if I need to do it." (P3)

Wireframe and microcopy notes (concrete):
- Inline delta row: On route -> variant pick, add a compact delta row: \"est. latency: 120ms (+40ms) · est. cost: $0.003/token (+12%)\". Keep numbers rounded. Add tooltip that explains estimation method.
- Variant badge taxonomy: Replace label \"variant\" with taxonomy: \"architecture / precision / optics\" (e.g., \"Llama-3-8B · int8 · v2-opt\") to reduce ambiguity. Keep single-line summary visible.
- Persistent change card: For any route-level change, display a non-modal persistent card at top of route page summarizing change, with primary CTA: \"Undo\" and secondary: \"View diff\". Card auto-dismiss after 10 minutes unless pinned.
- Fallback transparency panel: Create small panel on route activity: shows last 3 routing events (time, from-model -> to-model, reason). Default collapsed.
- Cost-safeguard setup: When creating a safeguard, show historical baseline and an estimate of how the safeguard would affect throughput/latency using a checkbox \"show expected perf impact\".

Observed errors and safety concerns:
- P5 inadvertently selected a quantized model when they meant a different architecture due to unclear naming. Risk: production degraded responses. Severity: high. Remediation: clearer taxonomy and confirmation for cross-precision switches.
- P1 kept toggling autoscale aggressively because console didn't show expected concurrency limits per GPU type. Risk: cost shock. Severity: medium. Remediation: show per-node throughput estimate at the time of policy edit.

Backlog grooming (proposed tickets with priority and notes):
- JIRA-3491 (P0): Variant taxonomy change + microcopy edits (owner: Priya). Add small migration doc for existing routes. Rationale: prevents high-severity mis-selection.
- JIRA-3492 (P1): Inline delta row for variant selection (owner: Liam). Needs small estimation service hook (backend change). Quick win: mock with heuristic if backend hook delayed.
- JIRA-3493 (P1): Persistent change card + undo affordance (owner: Maya). UX + frontend only, low-risk.
- JIRA-3494 (P2): Fallback transparency panel (owner: Diego). Integrate with tracing logs; MVP: show simple event list with links to traces.
- JIRA-3495 (P2): Cost-safeguard perf-impact preview (owner: product metrics). Requires sampling-based estimate.

Prioritization rationale:
- Triage high for taxonomy/microcopy edits (3491) because the observed mistake had immediate production impact in two sessions and is easy to ship.
- Inline deltas (3492) scored high on confidence but medium cost (backend). Can be A/B tested; consider client-side heuristic first.
- Undo card (3493) is a low-effort confidence booster and should ship quickly as a behavioral nudge.

Hypotheses and experiments to run post-change:
- H1: Adding inline delta (latency/cost) will reduce variant-change hesitation by 40% and time-on-task by 25% (measured in followup usability sessions + event rate of rollbacks).
- H2: Variant taxonomy clarity reduces accidental precision/architecture swaps by 80% (measured by fewer rollback support tickets referencing \"wrong quantization\").
- H3: Persistent undo card reduces support escalations for route-change incidents by 30% in first 2 weeks.

Metrics and instrumentation needed:
- Instrument: variant_change_confirmed, variant_change_undo, variant_change_view_diff, fallback_event_shown, fallback_event_acted, cost_safeguard_created, cost_safeguard_preview_used.
- Add tags to events for \"delta_viewed\" and \"delta_tooltip_open\" to measure discovery.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Estimation accuracy: how often will estimated delta be off? If frequently inaccurate, it could reduce trust. Need backend sampling plan and clear phrasing (\"estimated\") and confidence band.
- Undo semantics: How far back should undo reach? Only last route change or a longer sequence? Simpler = last change.
- GDPR/PII: Should the fallback event panel show request IDs? Risk of exposing customer data in UI; default to non-identifying IDs with link to audit logs (if permitted).

Next steps and owners (2-week sprint plan):
- Week 1: Ship microcopy taxonomy patch and small name-change migration guide (Priya). Create design tokens in Figma and ask content for microcopy variants.
- Week 1: Prototype inline delta with client-side heuristic (Liam). Build mock evaluation page for internal testing.
- Week 2: Implement persistent change card frontend and local undo (Maya + FE). Add metrics for undo events.
- Week 2: Draft experiment plan and instrumentation ticket (Diego + product analytics).

Appendix (session snapshots / low-fi sketches):
- Sketch A: Route detail with variant dropdown + delta row (annotated)
- Sketch B: Persistent change card with Undo + View diff
- Sketch C: Fallback transparency collapsed panel (three-line summary)

Notes to self:
- Keep prototype lightweight; stakeholders want to see UX flow before backend work.
- Flag JIRA-3491 for urgent review in triage meeting next Tue.

End of note.
